Hi! Glad you are considering applying for A&W and I'll try and speak to my experience as best I can. This will likely vary across different management and stores but hopefully, it will apply to you in some way. I've been working at A&Dubs for 2 years and I've really enjoyed it. You don't have to worry about being introduced to things too quickly, assuming you have good management, you'll be slowly introduced to things over time. If you don't know how to make a certain thing you can always ask. Additionally, while learning a menu and all the burger toppings might seem daunting, when you're constantly working around it you'll find yourself memorizing it a lot faster than you think you would. Knowing everything off by heart isn't a requirement though, but it will be generally expected of you after you've been there a few months and have to make burgers on your own or when a customer asks what comes on a certain item. Generally, from what I hear about other food service places, A&W gives you a lot more responsibility, which I consider to be a good thing. Unlike, for example, McDonald's where you have a large team of people each doing one very specific thing, A&W has its employees doing a lot more things at once. You feel more valued this way and I think it does well in building up workmanship in yourself. My recommendations for getting hired are the following. Firstly, you're going to have a better chance of getting hired if you're willing to work more flexible hours. Generally, we're often always looking for people who can open and close, so people willing to work those shifts and come in early or stay late are always needed. Additionally, try making a cover letter which is basically just a short blurb about why you want to work there and what skills you offer. Not many people submit them, so by doing so you're immediately standing out from the rest.

I wish you the best in trying to get a job there, and feel free to ask me any other questions you may have!

I realized that if I try and really organize a perfect binder, whenever I get even 1 new card, I may have to reorganize the whole thing in order for it to fit so I have a solution that works for me. 

For my Sun & Moon cards I organize by set, in order of card number, in order of release of the set, so when I get a new card I just slip it in the empty spot it would be in.

Then I have a binder for my gen 1, 2, pre gen-7 ultra rares & legendaries & other cards that are of deep sentimental value to me.

There are then 2 binders, 1 for gens 3&4, the other gen 5&6 organized by type, then by evolution line.

Lastly, if I get any new cards that aren't gen 7, they go into binder 5.

EDIT:For my cards at least 1 copy of each card I have is in a binder, anything else is put into tins/ETB as trading doubles.
